Planning Commission, October 25, 2023  Page 2 of 2
   MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING
  NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA
  OCTOBER 11, 2023

Chair Barragan called the special hybrid meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the Norwalk City
Hall, Council Chambers and via video/teleconference pursuant to the provisions of
Assembly Bill 361. Responding to roll call in person were Commissioner Apodaca,
Commissioner Garcia and Chair Barragan and, via Zoom, Commissioner Navas and Vice
Chair Lopez. Also present were Gloria V. Ramirez, Deputy City Attorney; Jill Ann Arabe,
Development Services Manager, Gabriel R. Salazar, Senior Planner; Andrew Arellano,
Assistant Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann, Administrative Secretary.

MEETING MINUTES

The Planning Commission approved the minutes of the Special Meeting of September
27, 2023.

CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 2023-03
DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST NO. 2023-08
Crystal Cyprian and Joy Cyprian, Joy’s Children’s Learning Center (“Applicant”); a
request to permit a child care facility within an existing 2,785 square foot building and
2,797 square foot building for ancillary storage on a 0.37 acre site. The subject property
is generally known as 11004 Adoree Street, located on the southeast corner of Adoree
Street and Studebaker Road (also known as Assessor’s Parcel Number (“APN”) 8050-
026-001), in the Commercial and Office (C and O) zone. The project includes a request
for:
(1) Conditional Use Permit: To permit a child care facility within an existing 2,785 square
  foot single-story building; and
(2) Director Approval Request No. 2023-08: To allow an eighteen (18) percent reduction
  (three spaces) from the required number of parking spaces; and
(3) Environmental: Consider and find that the project is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15301
  (Existing Facilities).

Deputy City Attorney Ramirez stated that, for the record, Chair Barragan was not
present at the last Planning Commission meeting; however, they want the record to
reflect that she was provided with all the materials for this meeting and the previous
meeting. In response to Deputy City Attorney Ramirez’ question whether she had a
chance to review that material, Chair Barragan answered in the affirmative, and she
indicated that she is prepared to continue with this item tonight.

Chair Barragan opened the continued public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Senior Planner Salazar
presented a report stating that at the September 27, 2023 public hearing, the applicant
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 2
Minutes of the Special Meeting  October 11, 2023

and property owner asked that Condition of Approval No. 4 for the Conditional Use
Permit be modified; that additional language was considered by inserting the phrase
“but not limited to” the appropriate site improvements listed; that traffic flow and safety
concerns were shared by a few of the Commissioners; that the property owner indicated
that traffic accidents occurred late at night and that they were not associated with the
subject site; that a motion was made to deny the project and a motion was made to
approve the project; that, as both motions failed by a 2-2 vote, the Commission, by a
4-0 vote acted to continue the item to the October 11, 2023 meeting to allow the full
Commission to be present. Further, he stated that Commissioner Garcia provided
suggested Conditions of Approval that have been shared with the Commission and the
applicant; and that staff recommends approval of the project subject to the Conditions
of Approval contained in Resolution Nos. 23-26 and 23-27.

In response to Commissioner Garcia’s comment if staff discussed with the applicants
the proposed revised language, Senior Planner Salazar indicated that they are
supportive of the revised conditions.

The applicants, Joy Cyprian and her daughter Crystal Cyprian, stated that they are
thankful to be here with the full Commission present; and that Crystal is going to remind
the Commission of the demographics and why they chose Norwalk as their chosen
location.

Crystal Cyprian Jacob stated that she is the co-owner of Joy’s Children’s Learning
Center; that they have a strong passion for early childhood education; that they have
over thirty plus years of experience; that there is a lack of early childhood education
facilities; that according to the United States Business Bureau there are 7,095 children
five years and younger in the City of Norwalk; that, currently, there are only three infant
childcare facilities that can support a total of 53 infants in Norwalk; that there are a total
of 25 licensed pre-school centers that can only support a total of 1,548 preschoolers;
that these statistics illustrate the need for Joy’s Children’s Learning Center which is a
quality and safe program; that there are 5,494 children that would go without child care
services in the City of Norwalk due to the lack of child care centers; that they are
providing a service to children and families within the community; that they focus on the
whole child, the environment at home and at school; that they provide nutritional needs
as there is food insecurity with young families; that with their program, they provide a
free breakfast, lunch and snacks for the children; that in closing, she would like the
Commission to know that this is the main reason why they chose Norwalk; and she
thanked the Commission for taking their request into consideration.

Ben Shen, a member of the ownership group, stated that they are very much in
agreement with the wording change to Resolution No. 23-26 which they received today;
that the two biggest issues brought up by the Commissioners at the last meeting were
traffic and safety which they also agree with; that Commissioner Apodaca brought up a
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 3
Minutes of the Special Meeting  October 11, 2023

day care center, the TLC Learning Center, that is located closer to her residence; that
he spoke with them and learned that they currently have four classes of 24 children in
each class; that, including staff, there are over one hundred people in that learning
center; that the child care center they are proposing is for a maximum of 20 children
with approximately five to six staff members; that they believe that the traffic impact at
the subject site would be minimal; that traffic safety would not be an issue; that they are
providing plenty of safeguards, including cameras and people in place during pickup
and drop off times.

Kevin Lee stated that he is the real estate broker who put this children learning center
lease together for the Cyprians, and that he is also one of the representatives of the
property owner; that, first, he would like to thank the Commission for the opportunity to
speak with them tonight; that he would like to share some of his thoughts; that he
understands the concerns with Joy’s Children’s Learning Center occupying the site,
mainly affecting the traffic flow in the area; that they are aware that the City staff has
spent months on the traffic study; that they have given the applicant positive feedback
and support as well as recommending approval of the project; that the study shows that
there is going to be a minimum impact to the area; that, as the Conditions of Approval
indicate, the traffic situation is going to be closely monitored by the City; that he has
known the Cyprians for about a year now and that they are the kindest persons he has
ever known; that their mission is to help Norwalk families and their children; that there
are many children in Norwalk who are in need of this opportunity; that the Cyprians have
over thirty years of experience of running this facility and providing quality care for the
community; that the landlord has been investing a lot of money and time to support the
applicants; that they are thankful for all the hard work done by the City staff on this
project; and that he sincerely hopes that the Commission looks favorably on this
application.

Commissioner Apodaca thanked the applicants for returning tonight. Further, she
stated that she applauds the applicants’ thirty years of loyalty and dedication to children,
which is a wonderful accomplishment; that she would like them to become a part of the
Norwalk community; that her only concern is with the location as the vicinity, in general,
is dangerous; that, unfortunately, they have seen this repeatedly over the last two
months, and twice last week; and that she does not want to see anything bad happen
at that location.

Commissioner Garcia inquired as to the distance from the 105 freeway exit to the
proposed location on Adoree.

Mr. Shen stated that they have two properties, one on Studebaker where the medical
center is located, and the other one on Adoree; that the two incidents that happened
this past week were on the Studebaker side; that it is completely on separate sides of
the street; that during the past eight months while they were developing these
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 4
Minutes of the Special Meeting  October 11, 2023

properties, they have had multiple issues on Studebaker and zero issues on Adoree;
that Studebaker is in direct line of exit from the 105 freeway which is causing these
issues; that they have been working with Planning, Public Safety and addressing this
issue with Caltrans in trying to get extra lights put in, signage, etc. to help them protect
their other investment; and that, again, the child care facility is completely on separate
sides of the street with zero incidents on Adoree.

Commissioner Garcia shared that for him the bigger issue is not so much the danger of
a car landing at the preschool, but the traffic circulation in a residential neighborhood.

Mr. Shen agreed with Commissioner Garcia’s comments, and he indicated that this is
why they have addressed that issue as well with designated drop off spots within the
parking lot and drop off times with assistance from parking staff who will be out there
during drop off and pickup times; that they also expect some foot traffic from the
neighboring homes; and that the number of cars will be minimal and staggered.

In response to Commissioner Garcia’s question if they had a chance to look at the
proposed language on Condition of Approval No. 4, Mr. Shen replied that they reviewed
it and agree with it; that their concern is the same as that of the Commission in that
safety is number one; that there is a need to revisit the traffic impacts and that they
would work with the City on a resolution, but that they feel strongly that it would never
reach that point.

Commissioner Garcia stated that the applicants collaborate with the City; that there will
be an evaluation of the traffic impacts in six months with Public Safety being involved;
that the City is trying to be a good neighbor; that the whole purpose is to improve traffic
mitigation in the area and provide safety for the residents and the children.

Commissioner Apodaca shared that, normally, the Commission would be provided with
a report from Public Safety.

Development Services Manager Arabe replied that Public Safety did not provide
anything in writing, which is why some of the conditions that they have shared are
intended to address some of those concerns; that in terms of a full report on the number
of accidents, except for the two recent ones, they do not have those numbers generated
as the data is not necessarily associated to the subject site; that if the Commission is
interested in more of that data to be collected, staff would ask Public Safety to provide
that information.

Commissioner Navas stated that he does not know why this property is being penalized
when the accidents are happening on the other side of the street; that they owe it to the
City to have a day care facility; that the applicants should be given the opportunity to
operate this facility with the conditions set forth; and that he is in favor of the project.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 5
Minutes of the Special Meeting  October 11, 2023

Vice Chair Lopez shared that she has no questions or comments at this time.

Chair Barragan stated that she has the same concerns expressed regarding the traffic
impact to the area.

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Barragan closed
the public hearing.

Chair Barragan thanked the applicants and staff for all the information provided.
Further, she stated that she hopes that it does not seem that the Commission is
penalizing the applicants; and that the Commission is an advisory body to the City
Council.

It was moved by Commissioner Garcia and seconded by Commissioner Navas to: (1)
Adopt Resolution No. 23-26 to approve Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-03 subject to
the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”, and with a modification to the
language provided in Condition No. 4; and (2) Adopt Resolution No. 23-27 to approve
Director Approval Request No. 2023-08 subject to the Conditions of Approval contained
in Exhibit “A”; and (3) Considered and found that the project is exempt from the
California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines, Section
15301 (Existing Facilities).

ON ROLL CALL VOTE
AYES:  Commissioner Garcia and Commissioner Navas
NOES: Commissioner Apodaca, Vice Chair Lopez and Chair Barragan
ABSENT: None

As the motion to approve failed by a vote of 2-3, it was moved by Commissioner
Apodaca and seconded by Vice Chair Lopez to direct staff to prepare resolutions for
denial for Planning Commission consideration at the meeting of October 25, 2023.

ON ROLL CALL VOTE
AYES:  Commissioner Apodaca, Vice Chair Lopez and Chair Barragan
NOES: Commissioner Garcia and Commissioner Navas
ABSENT: None

ZONING TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2023-01
ZONE CHANGE NO. 2023-01
To amend various sections of Title 17 of the Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC) as it relates
to the Automobile Parking (“P”) zone, and to remove the zoning designation of
Automobile Parking (“P”) on real property located throughout the City of Norwalk.
Environmental: Consider and find the project exempt from CEQA pursuant to Section
15061(b)(3).
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 6
Minutes of the Special Meeting  October 11, 2023

Chair Barragan opened the continued public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Assistant Planner Arellano
presented a report stating that this item was continued from the September 27, 2023
meeting due to issues with noticing; that the request is to amend various sections of
Title 17 of the Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC) as it relates to the Automobile Parking
(“P”) zone and to remove the P zone from the zoning map; that the P zone was originally
adopted in 1959 by Ordinance No. 114 to serve as a buffer for commercial or industrial
uses; that there are 275 parcels that contain a P zoning either exclusively or within the
parcel; that the P zone primarily prohibits construction of a building; however, 43 existing
sites contain structures; that the proposed update will simplify the list of permitted land
uses and zones, minimize conflicts between zoning code requirements, and serve as a
proactive approach of enhancing economic development; that no parking will be
removed from the streets; that out of the 275 parcels five will remain non-conforming
after this change; that this change aligns with the General Plan’s objective to support
the City’s physical and economic growth; that this change also allows property owners
to expand their buildings and thus encourage more development; and that staff
recommends that the Commission recommend approval of the project to City Council.

Commissioner Apodaca indicated that she received a notice of this item at her residence
and she asked for clarification as to whether or not she can participate in this discussion.

Deputy City Attorney Ramirez shared that the rule is if there is a financial interest in the
action that will be taken tonight there may be a likelihood of a conflict of interest;
however, given that everybody will be impacted, the rule is that she can proceed if she
feels comfortable enough.

Since there were no persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Barragan closed the
public hearing.

As none of the Planning Commissioners voiced any comments, it was moved by
Commissioner Apodaca and seconded by Vice Chair Lopez to: (1) Adopt Resolution
No. 23-28, to recommend approval to City Council for Zoning Text Amendment (ZTA)
No. 2023-01; and (2) Adopt Resolution No. 23-29, to recommend approval to City
Council for Zone Change (ZC) No. 2023-01; and (3) Consider and find that the project
is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA
Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3).

ON ROLL CALL VOTE
AYES:  Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Garcia, Commissioner Navas,
  Vice Chair Lopez and Chair Barragan
NOES:  None
ABSENT: None
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 7
Minutes of the Special Meeting  October 11, 2023

ZONING TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2023-02
A request initiated by city staff to amend various sections of Title 17 of the Norwalk
Municipal Code (NMC) to streamline the Precise Development Plan (PDP) process by
authorizing the Director of Community Development to make final decisions and/or
recommend Planning Commission approval of Precise Development Plans.
Environmental: Consider and find that the proposed Zoning Text Amendment is exempt
from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines,
Section 15061(b)(3).

Chair Barragan opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Assistant Planner Arellano
presented a report stating that this is a staff-initiated project; that the Precise
Development Plan requirement was adopted by Ordinance No. 757 in 1972; that staff
intends to streamline the Precise Development Plan process by authorizing the
Community Development Director to review and approve projects; that this project is
exempt pursuant to California Environmental Quality Act Guidelines 15061(b)(3) as it will
not involve any construction nor have a significant effect on the environment; that the
project aligns with the General Plan policies and objectives of upgrading infrastructure
and services to support the City’s physical and economic growth, and establishing a
positive image for Norwalk as a growing city; that the project will also reduce the
associated processing time for the Precise Development Plans which will help to promote
a positive image of the development process in Norwalk; that additional benefits include
the redevelopment of vacant properties and the creation of more opportunities for
employment and goods and services; that the proposed amendment will also allow the
Director of Community Development to refer a project to the Planning Commission for
discretionary action; that, additionally, if a Precise Development Plan were submitted
concurrently with a discretionary application such as a Conditional Use Permit, both
applications would be subject to review and approval by the Planning Commission, and
that staff recommends that the Commission adopt Resolution No. 23-30 to recommend
approval to City Council.

In response to Commissioner Apodaca’s inquiry as to the criteria that would have
applications come before the Planning Commission, Assistant Planner Arellano shared
that if a Conditional Use Permit is required concurrently with a Precise Development Plan,
then those applications would be reviewed by the Planning Commission; and that review
by the Director will apply to projects that are permitted in the zone, conform to
development standards in the Norwalk Municipal Code, and solely require a Precise
Development Plan.

Since there were no persons wishing to present testimony and no other comments were
voiced by the Commission, Chair Barragan closed the public hearing.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 8
Minutes of the Special Meeting  October 11, 2023

It was moved by Commissioner Garcia and seconded by Commissioner Navas to: (1)
Adopt Resolution No. 23-30 to recommend approval to City Council for Zoning Text
Amendment No. 2023-02 providing the Community Development Director authority to
initiate and make decisions on Precise Development Plans; and (2 Consider and find that
the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines, Section 15061(b)(3).

ON ROLL CALL VOTE
AYES:  Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Garcia, Commissioner Navas,
  Vice Chair Lopez and Chair Barragan
NOES:  None
ABSENT: None

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Development Services Manager Arabe shared that an application has been submitted for
a Raising Cane’s drive-through restaurant at the former CVS building at 12666
Studebaker Road, and that the project is anticipated to come before the Planning
Commission next month.

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business, the meeting adjourned at 6:55 p.m.

  ROSA BARRAGAN, CHAIR

TO:  Planning Commission

FROM:  John P. Ramirez, AICP, Director of Community Development

BY:  Gabriel Salazar, MSPA, Senior Planner

SUBJECT: Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-03 / Director Approval Request No. 2023-
  08 to permit a child care facility within an existing 2,785 square foot building
  and 2,797 square foot building for ancillary storage on a 0.37-acre-site.
  Environmental: Consider and find the project exempt from CEQA pursuant
  to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities). The subject property is 11004
  Adoree Street, located on the southeast corner of Adoree Street and
  Studebaker Road.

RECOMMENDATION

That the Planning Commission:

1. Adopt Resolution Nos. 23-26 and 23-27 to deny Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-03
  and Director Approval Request No. 2023-08, respectively.

BACKGROUND

Based upon testimony and discussion at the Planning Commission meeting on October
11, 2023, the Planning Commission directed staff to prepare resolutions for denial for
CUP No. 2023-03 and DAR No. 2023-08. The minutes for October 11, 2023, are also
attached.

ATTACHMENTS

A. Resolution No. 23-26 (Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-03)
B. Resolution No. 23-27 (Director Approval Request No. 2023-08)
C. Planning Commission minutes for October 11, 2023
   ATTACHMENT A

  NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION
  RESOLUTION NO. 23-26

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA, SETTING FORTH ITS FINDINGS OF FACT AND
  DECISION RELATIVE TO THE DENIAL OF CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO.
  2023-03

  WHEREAS, Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No. 2023-03 was submitted by Crystal and Joy
Cyprian, Joy’s Children Learning Center, for 11004 Adoree Street (“Subject Property”); also
known as Assessor’s Parcel Number (“APN”) 8056-026-001, a request to permit a childcare
facility on a 0.37-acre site; and

  WHEREAS, Director Approval Request (DAR) No. 2023-08 was filed in conjunction with
this request; and

  WHEREAS, the purpose and intent of requiring a conditional use permit is to ensure that
compatibility is maintained between a conditional use on a specific site, and other existing and
future land uses on adjacent and surrounding properties; and

  WHEREAS, Section 17.02.210.A of the Norwalk Municipal Code authorizes the Planning
Commission to grant a conditional use permit and impose such conditions as it deems necessary
and reasonable to protect the best interests of the surrounding property or neighborhood and to
ensure compliance with the Zoning Ordinance and the General Plan; and

  WHEREAS, Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-03 has been reviewed by the Planning
Commission on October 11, 2023, at a duly noticed public hearing; and

  WHEREAS, oral testimony and written comments related to the application were received
and considered at the public hearing; and

  WHEREAS, all legal prerequisites to the adoption of this Resolution have occurred.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. The project will be detrimental to the public health, safety, and welfare. Based
upon testimony shared during the public hearing, the project location is not suitable for the
childcare operation due to its proximity to a dangerous intersection and along a major street with
a history of numerous vehicle accidents. Because the repeated number of vehicle related
incidents nearby is high, the potential for vehicular accidents as a result of the use will magnify
the existing traffic conditions.

  Section 2. The project will have negative impacts on the surrounding neighborhood due
to its reduction in parking and potential for adding traffic congestion along a major street with a
history of numerous vehicle accidents and near a dangerous intersection. As proposed, the use
will not serve to benefit the community.

  Section 3. The Planning Commission of the City of Norwalk, State of California, does
hereby deny Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-03 without prejudice.
   PASSED, APPROVED AND ADOPTED BY THE NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION
on this 25th day of October 2023.

  ROSA BARRAGAN, CHAIR
  NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION

Chair Barragan called the special hybrid meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the Norwalk City
Hall, Council Chambers and via video/teleconference pursuant to the provisions of
Assembly Bill 361. Responding to roll call in person were Commissioner Apodaca,
Commissioner Garcia and Chair Barragan and, via Zoom, Commissioner Navas and Vice
Chair Lopez. Also present were Gloria V. Ramirez, Deputy City Attorney; Jill Ann Arabe,
Development Services Manager, Gabriel R. Salazar, Senior Planner; Andrew Arellano,
Assistant Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann, Administrative Secretary.

MEETING MINUTES

The Planning Commission approved the minutes of the Special Meeting of September
27, 2023.

CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 2023-03
DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST NO. 2023-08
Crystal Cyprian and Joy Cyprian, Joy’s Children’s Learning Center (“Applicant”); a
request to permit a child care facility within an existing 2,785 square foot building and
2,797 square foot building for ancillary storage on a 0.37 acre site. The subject property
is generally known as 11004 Adoree Street, located on the southeast corner of Adoree
Street and Studebaker Road (also known as Assessor’s Parcel Number (“APN”) 8050-
026-001), in the Commercial and Office (C and O) zone. The project includes a request
for:
(1) Conditional Use Permit: To permit a child care facility within an existing 2,785 square
  foot single-story building; and
(2) Director Approval Request No. 2023-08: To allow an eighteen (18) percent reduction
  (three spaces) from the required number of parking spaces; and
(3) Environmental: Consider and find that the project is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15301
  (Existing Facilities).

Deputy City Attorney Ramirez stated that, for the record, Chair Barragan was not
present at the last Planning Commission meeting; however, they want the record to
reflect that she was provided with all the materials for this meeting and the previous
meeting. In response to Deputy City Attorney Ramirez’ question whether she had a
chance to review that material, Chair Barragan answered in the affirmative, and she
indicated that she is prepared to continue with this item tonight.

Chair Barragan opened the continued public hearing.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 2

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Senior Planner Salazar
presented a report stating that at the September 27, 2023 public hearing, the applicant
and property owner asked that Condition of Approval No. 4 for the Conditional Use
Permit be modified; that additional language was considered by inserting the phrase
“but not limited to” the appropriate site improvements listed; that traffic flow and safety
concerns were shared by a few of the Commissioners; that the property owner indicated
that traffic accidents occurred late at night and that they were not associated with the
subject site; that a motion was made to deny the project and a motion was made to
approve the project; that, as both motions failed by a 2-2 vote, the Commission, by a
4-0 vote acted to continue the item to the October 11, 2023 meeting to allow the full
Commission to be present. Further, he stated that Commissioner Garcia provided
suggested Conditions of Approval that have been shared with the Commission and the
applicant; and that staff recommends approval of the project subject to the Conditions
of Approval contained in Resolution Nos. 23-26 and 23-27.

In response to Commissioner Garcia’s comment if staff discussed with the applicants
the proposed revised language, Senior Planner Salazar indicated that they are
supportive of the revised conditions.

The applicants, Joy Cyprian and her daughter Crystal Cyprian, stated that they are
thankful to be here with the full Commission present; and that Crystal is going to remind
the Commission of the demographics and why they chose Norwalk as their chosen
location.

Crystal Cyprian Jacob stated that she is the co-owner of Joy’s Children’s Learning
Center; that they have a strong passion for early childhood education; that they have
over thirty plus years of experience; that there is a lack of early childhood education
facilities; that according to the United States Business Bureau there are 7,095 children
five years and younger in the City of Norwalk; that, currently, there are only three infant
childcare facilities that can support a total of 53 infants in Norwalk; that there are a total
of 25 licensed pre-school centers that can only support a total of 1,548 preschoolers;
that these statistics illustrate the need for Joy’s Children’s Learning Center which is a
quality and safe program; that there are 5,494 children that would go without child care
services in the City of Norwalk due to the lack of child care centers; that they are
providing a service to children and families within the community; that they focus on the
whole child, the environment at home and at school; that they provide nutritional needs
as there is food insecurity with young families; that with their program, they provide a
free breakfast, lunch and snacks for the children; that in closing, she would like the
Commission to know that this is the main reason why they chose Norwalk; and she
thanked the Commission for taking their request into consideration.

Ben Shen, a member of the ownership group, stated that they are very much in
agreement with the wording change to Resolution No. 23-26 which they received today;
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 3

that the two biggest issues brought up by the Commissioners at the last meeting were
traffic and safety which they also agree with; that Commissioner Apodaca brought up a
day care center, the TLC Learning Center, that is located closer to her residence; that
he spoke with them and learned that they currently have four classes of 24 children in
each class; that, including staff, there are over one hundred people in that learning
center; that the child care center they are proposing is for a maximum of 20 children
with approximately five to six staff members; that they believe that the traffic impact at
the subject site would be minimal; that traffic safety would not be an issue; that they are
providing plenty of safeguards, including cameras and people in place during pickup
and drop off times.

Kevin Lee stated that he is the real estate broker who put this children learning center
lease together for the Cyprians, and that he is also one of the representatives of the
property owner; that, first, he would like to thank the Commission for the opportunity to
speak with them tonight; that he would like to share some of his thoughts; that he
understands the concerns with Joy’s Children’s Learning Center occupying the site,
mainly affecting the traffic flow in the area; that they are aware that the City staff has
spent months on the traffic study; that they have given the applicant positive feedback
and support as well as recommending approval of the project; that the study shows that
there is going to be a minimum impact to the area; that, as the Conditions of Approval
indicate, the traffic situation is going to be closely monitored by the City; that he has
known the Cyprians for about a year now and that they are the kindest persons he has
ever known; that their mission is to help Norwalk families and their children; that there
are many children in Norwalk who are in need of this opportunity; that the Cyprians have
over thirty years of experience of running this facility and providing quality care for the
community; that the landlord has been investing a lot of money and time to support the
applicants; that they are thankful for all the hard work done by the City staff on this
project; and that he sincerely hopes that the Commission looks favorably on this
application.

Commissioner Apodaca thanked the applicants for returning tonight. Further, she
stated that she applauds the applicants’ thirty years of loyalty and dedication to children,
which is a wonderful accomplishment; that she would like them to become a part of the
Norwalk community; that her only concern is with the location as the vicinity, in general,
is dangerous; that, unfortunately, they have seen this repeatedly over the last two
months, and twice last week; and that she does not want to see anything bad happen
at that location.

Commissioner Garcia inquired as to the distance from the 105 freeway exit to the
proposed location on Adoree.

Mr. Shen stated that they have two properties, one on Studebaker where the medical
center is located, and the other one on Adoree; that the two incidents that happened

this past week were on the Studebaker side; that it is completely on separate sides of
the street; that during the past eight months while they were developing these
properties, they have had multiple issues on Studebaker and zero issues on Adoree;
that Studebaker is in direct line of exit from the 105 freeway which is causing these
issues; that they have been working with Planning, Public Safety and addressing this
issue with Caltrans in trying to get extra lights put in, signage, etc. to help them protect
their other investment; and that, again, the child care facility is completely on separate
sides of the street with zero incidents on Adoree.

Commissioner Garcia shared that for him the bigger issue is not so much the danger of
a car landing at the preschool, but the traffic circulation in a residential neighborhood.

Mr. Shen agreed with Commissioner Garcia’s comments, and he indicated that this is
why they have addressed that issue as well with designated drop off spots within the
parking lot and drop off times with assistance from parking staff who will be out there
during drop off and pickup times; that they also expect some foot traffic from the
neighboring homes; and that the number of cars will be minimal and staggered.

In response to Commissioner Garcia’s question if they had a chance to look at the
proposed language on Condition of Approval No. 4, Mr. Shen replied that they reviewed
it and agree with it; that their concern is the same as that of the Commission in that
safety is number one; that there is a need to revisit the traffic impacts and that they
would work with the City on a resolution, but that they feel strongly that it would never
reach that point.

Commissioner Garcia stated that the applicants collaborate with the City; that there will
be an evaluation of the traffic impacts in six months with Public Safety being involved;
that the City is trying to be a good neighbor; that the whole purpose is to improve traffic
mitigation in the area and provide safety for the residents and the children.

Commissioner Apodaca shared that, normally, the Commission would be provided with
a report from Public Safety.

Development Services Manager Arabe replied that Public Safety did not provide
anything in writing, which is why some of the conditions that they have shared are
intended to address some of those concerns; that in terms of a full report on the number
of accidents, except for the two recent ones, they do not have those numbers generated
as the data is not necessarily associated to the subject site; that if the Commission is
interested in more of that data to be collected, staff would ask Public Safety to provide
that information.

Commissioner Navas stated that he does not know why this property is being penalized
when the accidents are happening on the other side of the street; that they owe it to the

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Barragan closed

It was moved by Commissioner Garcia and seconded by Commissioner Navas to: (1)
Adopt Resolution No. 23-26 to approve Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-03 subject to
the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”, and with a modification to the
language provided in Condition No. 4; and (2) Adopt Resolution No. 23-27 to approve
Director Approval Request No. 2023-08 subject to the Conditions of Approval contained
in Exhibit “A”; and (3) Considered and found that the project is exempt from the
California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines, Section
15301 (Existing Facilities).
